title: Ramavtar Singh v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Sunita Agarwal, J.; Vipin Chandra Dixit, J.
disposition: Writ disposed of; remaining computation dispute relegated to Clause 6.5, with no coercive measures pending a speaking order.
headnote: After a Consumer Forum had set aside prior electricity bills and directed revision without interest or surcharge, the Allahabad High Court declined to interfere with alleged recovery. Finding no live recovery as on date, it left any remaining computation dispute to the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and directed that if such an objection is filed, no coercive measures shall be taken until a reasoned speaking order is passed under intimation to the consumer.
facts: Ramavtar Singh alleged the department had violated a Consumer Forum order dated 11 November 2022, which set aside earlier electricity bills and directed fresh bills from 2013 at average rate without interest or surcharge. The department produced a revised bill said to comply. The petitioner neither appended the Forum order nor showed whether the recovery citation predated it. Department counsel stated there was presently no recovery and undertook to advise withdrawal of citations sent to the Tehsil before the Forum order.

holding_units.topic: billing computation dispute — Clause 6.5 as alternate remedy
holding_units.holding: Where a Consumer Forum has already set aside prior electricity bills and directed revision, the licensee has issued a revised bill, and there is no live recovery as on date, the High Court will not interfere in writ. Any remaining dispute as to computation of the revised charges may be raised before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; if such objection is filed, no coercive measures shall be taken until a reasoned speaking order is passed under intimation to the consumer.

principle_tags.application: Writ challenging recovery after Consumer Forum-directed bill revision was disposed of without merits relief; remaining computation was left to Clause 6.5.
Petitioner left free to object to the current computation before the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.5, with a speaking-order requirement and a bar on coercive measures pending disposal.
Dispute as to computation of the revised electricity bill after the Consumer Forum order was treated as a Clause 6.5 statutory objection, not a matter for writ interference.

not_decided.point: Correctness of the revised electricity bill and the computation of charges
not_decided.note: Left to a Clause 6.5 objection before the Executive Engineer.

not_decided.point: Whether the recovery citation predated the Consumer Forum order of 11 November 2022
not_decided.note: Petitioner supplied no recovery-citation details; Court recorded that as on date there was no recovery.
